title: Every Word Could End This
tagline: A barricaded subject, a phone line that's the only thing connecting you to them, and a tactical team waiting on your read of the situation.

wake_up.text: On-call rotation. Your phone rings before you're fully awake — a barricade situation developing, a subject alone with a hostage, tactical already staging.

choices.text: Get a full briefing on the way before saying anything
Head out immediately and get briefed on arrival

scene_arrival.text: The scene is exactly as tense as it sounded on the phone — perimeter set, tactical team positioned, a command post already assembling the pieces of what happened.

choices.text: Get the full situational briefing

random_moment.text: The first minutes on scene have their own particular tension — a little different at every incident.

choices.text: A family member on scene gives you a useful detail about the subject
News vans are already setting up at the perimeter
The command post is unusually well organized this time

initial_contact.text: First phone contact with the subject — agitated, unpredictable, but talking. The hostage's status is still unconfirmed.

choices.text: Let them talk at length before saying much yourself
Establish clear structure to the conversation early

morning_negotiation.text: Ninety minutes in, the subject's tone has calmed somewhat, but they still won't confirm the hostage is unharmed.

choices.text: Continue building rapport

critical_moment.text: The subject suddenly goes quiet on the phone after a raised voice in the background — tactical is asking for a decision on entry, right now, and whatever you say next could be the thing that ends this calmly or ends it very differently.

choices.text: Stay on the line and keep talking, calm and steady
Request tactical hold their position while you assess
Recommend tactical entry immediately
Bring in a family member to speak, briefly, on the line

critical_outcome_stay.text: The subject comes back on the line after the longest thirty seconds of the day. The hostage is unharmed — the raised voice was the subject's own frustration, not violence. Staying calm on the line was exactly the right call.

choices.text: Continue toward a peaceful resolution

critical_outcome_hold.text: Tactical holds, and the pause gives the subject room to come back to the phone on their own terms — a careful, measured call that respects how fragile the moment actually was.

choices.text: Continue toward a peaceful resolution

critical_outcome_entry.text: Tactical entry resolves the situation, but it's a far more dangerous ending than the one that was quietly available if the line had just stayed open a little longer.

choices.text: Debrief the outcome

critical_outcome_family.text: The family member's voice on the line does something your own careful neutrality couldn't — the subject's tone shifts immediately, and the standoff's temperature drops with it.

choices.text: Continue toward a peaceful resolution

afternoon_resolution.text: Hours into the standoff, the subject is finally talking about how this ends, not just why it started.

choices.text: Stay patient and let them arrive at surrender on their own terms
Push more directly for a faster resolution

peaceful_end.text: The subject agrees to come out. The hostage is safe. Six hours after it started, the actual ending is almost anticlimactic — which is exactly what a good ending to this looks like.

choices.text: Oversee the safe conclusion

debrief.text: A full debrief with the tactical commander and your own supervisor — what worked, what nearly didn't, what the next negotiator on rotation should know.

choices.text: Be fully honest about every close moment, not just the good calls
Give the clean summary version

end_shift.text: The scene clears. Somewhere, a family is being reunited, and you're already back on the on-call list for whatever comes next.

choices.text: Head home

triumphant.title: Nobody Got Hurt
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, including the hardest one. This is the standoff other negotiators study.

steady_hand.title: Resolved Safely
steady_hand.blurb: No theatrics, no shortcuts — just patient, careful negotiation until it was actually over.

ordinary_day.title: Another Standoff Ended
ordinary_day.blurb: A long, tense day that ended the way it needed to. The on-call phone could ring again any minute.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the standoff, but you're not sure how. This kind of pressure has a real cost.

written_up.title: Incident Review
written_up.blurb: Something about today's tactical call is heading into a formal review. Everyone's safe. The department still wants to understand the decision.
